commit_reviews.summary: Greenfield session-1 commit establishing the TS/ts-jest test harness and lockfile for the SSG project without straying into implementation.

problems: deprecated @types/handlebars stub package added unnecessarily (handlebars ships its own types)
package.json dependency ordering not kept alphabetical
diff truncated so renderPage/resolution logic unverifiable
commit_reviews.summary: Introduces a clean Handlebar-based templating abstraction that replaces the hardcoded HTML builders and wires it through a new `--templates` CLI option.

problems: commits node_modules (60 files) and dist/ build artifacts
silently swallows rebuild errors in `catch (err) { // nop }`
user-controlled `req.url` joined onto outputDir without traversal guard
no error handling in the yargs `serve` handler
commit_reviews.summary: Competent, idiomatic integration — the new `serve` command mirrors the existing yargs command structure, reuses the `build({...})` API rather than duplicating logic, places the module in `src/serve.ts` per layout, and ships a matching 262-line test.

problems: DevServerPlugin tightly coupled to SSGEngine via setEngine
silent error swallowing in rebuild catch
commit_reviews.summary: The refactor cleanly extracts markdown, templates, and the dev server into built-in plugins with the exact lifecycle hooks from the session spec, leaving the engine to orchestrate the pipeline.

problems: duplicate BuildStats type in types.ts and cache.ts requiring alias hack in ssg.ts
(page as any)._fromCache magic-property casts in three files
caching logic scattered across markdown/template plugins
commit_reviews.summary: Caching is threaded through the existing BuildContext/plugin-hook architecture, but the implementation leaks `any` casts and duplicates shared types.

compounding_issues: S4 plugin refactor shipped with zero tests, leaving the largest behavioral rewrite (parse/render pipeline re-orchestrated around Plugin lifecycle hooks) unprotected; later sessions had no regression net

S3's serve.ts held WebSocket/chokidar logic inline and imported build() directly; S4 had to unwind it into dev-server-plugin, which then keeps a reference to SSGEngine via setEngine() — a tight plugin-engine coupling that persists through S5
S4 config loading uses require() on ssg.config.ts/.js from __dirname — fragile (needs ts-node in dev, resolves to dist in prod) and silently best-effort, a latent bug carried into S5

S5's incremental cache was bolted onto MarkdownPlugin specifically (dirty-check + cache read inside the plugin, skip counting in SSGEngine) instead of being a true cross-cutting infrastructure layer, using type-unsafe (page as any)._fromCache to bridge the abstraction
S1's hardcoded HTML shell and S2's standalone template-engine.ts both became dead code needing rework by S4's plugin extraction — minor but real duplication of effort
key_decisions: S4 plugin lifecycle architecture (SSGEngine + Plugin interface with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) plus config-driven plugin loading — the pivotal decision that reshaped the entire pipeline and framed sessions 5+
S2 adoption of a Handlebars template engine with layouts/partials/index templates, replacing S1's inline HTML strings and decoupling presentation from content parsing
S3 WebSocket live-reload dev server (chokidar + ws) integrating the build step into a persistent serve loop with static file serving and MIME handling
S5 content-addressed incremental cache (SHA256 source hashes + templatesHash manifest in .ssg-cache.json) exposed via --incremental/--clean CLI flags with BuildResult stats
S1 yargs-based CLI command structure (build, later serve) that stayed stable across all sessions, giving the story a consistent entry-point contract
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily: S1 delivered a clean but minimal yargs CLI + gray-matter/marked build pipeline with tests; S2 added a genuine Handlebars templating layer with layouts, partials, and an index template while keeping tests green; S3 integrated a live-reload dev server with its own test suite; S4 performed the boldest change — extracting a plugin engine — but skipped tests and introduced config-loading fragility and plugin-engine coupling; S5 added a substantial content-addressed incremental build feature with a 376-line test suite, yet its integration is the weakest seam of the whole story, leaking cache logic into the markdown plugin and relying on an any-cast flag. Net: competence and feature surface grew across the arc, while smell accumulation (type-unsafe seams, untested refactor, brittle config loading) rose most sharply in the final two sessions.
story_review.summary: A well-structured greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc with genuine architectural ambition, marred mainly by an untested S4 refactor and an incremental-cache feature in S5 that bypasses the plugin abstraction it was meant to extend.
